one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08. The stock fell 13.27% on 2026-10-09 ($171.31 to $148.58) [1] after SpaceX agreed to buy Grain's 800 MHz portfolio (up to 14 MHz paired), which needs FCC approval; New Street says the spectrum does not work with SpaceX's V1/V2 direct-to-device satellites, and Evercore calls it 'more of a coverage fix than a capacity solution' [5]. Light Reading reported T-Mobile down 'nearly 10%' in Friday morning trading [5], so the -13.27% close shows selling built through the day. Scheduled in the window: Q3 2026 results and call on 2026-10-28 [24]. Q3 is pre-guided soft: ~250k postpaid account adds (277k in Q2), service revenue ~$19.3B (+6%), Core Adj. EBITDA ~$9.4B (+8%, vs +12% in Q2), and a 'temporary elevated account churn profile' from the rate-plan modernization [23][16]. A print in line with that guide, plus reaffirmed 2026 guidance and the 2027 framework (maintained on 2026-09-03 [19]), is mostly priced in. The downside risk is churn above what the market assumes, or any softening of the 2027 targets; the upside is buyback pace at depressed prices and explicit 2027 reaffirmation. Verizon/AT&T Q3 dates and the FOMC meeting are not confirmed by me, so I do not weight them. Short-horizon regularities pull both ways: partial reversal after an event-driven gap on a threat that is mostly post-2027, against negative momentum at a 52-week low. Net: no directional edge, so I keep a near-symmetric distribution centred at ~$149 with ~10% monthly sigma (33%/3.5 = 9.4%, nudged up for the earnings event and the post-shock regime) and slightly fat tails. This is unchanged from round 1; the supervisor also left the 1-month ladder unchanged.

fair_value.method: Value at 2027-10-09, excluding ~$4.7 of dividends. Blend of P/E ($15.06 NTM EPS x 10.75x = $161.9, weight 0.40), FCF yield (2027 AFCF guidance low end $19.5B / 1,020M shares at 11.75% = $162.7, weight 0.35) and EV/EBITDA ($38.73B horizon LTM Core EBITDA x 6.6x less $89.1B net debt and $3.46B towers / 1,020M = $159.9, weight 0.25). 0.4 x 161.9 + 0.35 x 162.7 + 0.25 x 159.9 = 64.76 + 56.95 + 39.97 = $161.7, so ~$162 (round 1: $154).

inputs_detail.derivation: StockAnalysis/S&P Global average of 27 analysts, non-GAAP adjusted (the same basis as the forward P/Es of TMUS and every peer). It was partly set before the 2026-10-09 shock.

$14.44 x 0.97 = $14.01. A 3% haircut (4% in round 1). It now rests on primary evidence, not the Stocktwits recaps: consensus 2027 revenue growth is only +4.44% [2], so most of the +16.5% EPS growth needs margin and buybacks; ARPA grew only ~2% in Q2 [16]; Q3 guide slows Core EBITDA growth to +8% from +12% [23][15]. Sell-side target cuts (Scotiabank $217->$212, Bernstein Hold $220 [2]) are context only and do not set the size.
$14.01 x 1.10 = $15.41. 10% growth is below the +16.49% FY27 consensus growth [2] and the 17.03% 3Y forecast [1], reflecting deceleration with buyback support.

Core peer median 9.95x (8 verified peers; range 5.90x-15.46x). TMUS today 11.82x [1]. The premium is set by the verified US growth/multiple slope, not by sell-side opinion: VZ 8.23x on 6.99% 3Y EPS growth [25], T 9.20x on 11.06% [26], so 0.97x per 4.07pp of growth (0.24x per pp). Extending it to TMUS's 17.03% [1] gives 9.20 + 5.97 x 0.24 = 10.63x; I round to 10.75x (+8% vs the 9.95x median). That is a little above my round-1 10.5x, as the supervisor's growth-gap point suggests. I stop short of its 11x because part of the 17% is buyback-driven, consensus revenue growth is only 4.4% [2], and AMX trades at 10.9x on 18% growth [33]. [Citation gate 2026-10-12: the peer multiples cited here are StockAnalysis aggregator figures; the agent's value is kept as its view and the supervisor reconciliation uses the filings-based rebuild (core NTM P/E median 9.50x, EV/EBITDA 6.53x, FCF yield 12.29%).]

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027 AFCF $19.5B (low end of guidance) / 1,020M shares = $19.12 at an 11.75% yield (VZ 12.44%, T 11.62%) = $162.7

inputs_detail.derivation: Low end of the company's 2027 AFCF guidance of $19.5-20.5B (Feb 2026 8-K [18]), which is maintained per the 2026-09-03 8-K [19]. Using the low end is a $0.5B (2.5%) haircut to the $20.0B midpoint, because the Q3 guide is decelerating [23] and the SpaceX/cable competition may cost retention spend. In round 1 I wrongly labelled the same $19.5B an estimate.

1,072.7M at 2026-07-17 [17]. Remaining 2026 authorization: $18.2B [15] - $7.12B H1 buybacks [17] - ~$2.21B H1 dividends ($2.04/share [17] x ~1,085M avg shares, estimate) - $0.39B repurchased to Jul 17 [15] = ~$8.5B. Less H2 dividends ~$2.5B ($4.68/yr [1] / 4 x ~1,065M x 2) leaves ~$6.0B of buybacks, ~36M shares at ~$165 (judgment: much of it bought before the Oct 9 drop). For 2027 I read 'up to approximately $30B' of returns through 2027 [18] conservatively as 2026-27, so ~$11.8B in 2027, ~$4.8B of it dividends: ~$7.0B of buybacks, ~$5.25B by October, ~34M shares at ~$155. Plus ~10M of equity-comp issuance over five quarters (judgment). 1,072.7 - 36 - 34 + 10 = ~1,013M. I round up to 1,020M because spectrum spending may crowd out buybacks.

Verified US peers: VZ 12.44% [25], T 11.62% [26]. TMUS today 11.54% on ttm FCF of $18.40B [1]. TMUS's FCF is still growing (2026 guide $18.4-18.8B, 2027 $19.5-20.5B), so a yield at or below VZ's is justified. Given the SpaceX overhang I set it between T and VZ, not below T. 19.12 / 0.1175 = $162.7. In round 1 I used 8.0x P/FCF against a 10-peer P/FCF median whose non-US values I did not recheck this round, so I re-anchored to the two verified US peers. [Citation gate 2026-10-12: the peer multiples cited here are StockAnalysis aggregator figures; the agent's value is kept as its view and the supervisor reconciliation uses the filings-based rebuild (core NTM P/E median 9.50x, EV/EBITDA 6.53x, FCF yield 12.29%).]

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Horizon LTM Core Adj. EBITDA $38.73B (FY27 $39.2B = guidance low end less 2%) x 6.6x company basis = EV $255.6B; less net debt $89.1B (2.3x) and towers $3.46B; / 1,020M shares = $159.9

inputs_detail.derivation: Feb 2026 8-K [18]; maintained 2026-09-03 [19]; the CFO said on the Q2 call that the modernization 'sets us up to deliver against our 2027 guidance ambitions' [23].

$40.0B x 0.98 = $39.2B. A stated 2% haircut to the low end of guidance (3.4% to the $40.5B midpoint), up from round 1's unlabelled $38.8B. Why: hitting $40.0B needs +7.2% on the 2026 midpoint, while 2027 consensus revenue growth is +4.44% [2] and Q3 Core EBITDA growth slows to +8% [23]. $39.2B is still +5.1% on 2026.

Core peer median trailing EV/EBITDA 7.38x on the source's lease-inclusive basis. A +5% premium gives 7.75x, which is smaller than the P/E premium because EBITDA growth is slowing and the leverage is lease-heavy. Converting to the company basis: TMUS is 8.06x on the source [1] and (159.38 + 84.095 + 3.461) / 35.902 = 6.88x on the company basis [1][16], a ratio of 1.172. 7.75 / 1.172 = 6.61x, so 6.6x, about 4% below TMUS's current 6.88x. The multiple is applied to trailing (LTM) EBITDA, consistent with the trailing peer multiples. [Citation gate 2026-10-12: the peer multiples cited here are StockAnalysis aggregator figures; the agent's value is kept as its view and the supervisor reconciliation uses the filings-based rebuild (core NTM P/E median 9.50x, EV/EBITDA 6.53x, FCF yield 12.29%).]

Leverage held at 2.3x (Q2 actual [16]; below the 2.5x target [18]) x $38.73B = $89.1B. This is the company basis (excluding ~$29.1B of operating lease liabilities [17]), consistent with post-lease Core EBITDA.

bear.story: Q3/Q4 churn from the rate-plan modernization runs hotter than guided. Competition from cable MVNOs and a Starlink Mobile that the FCC approves forces retention spend. The 2027 targets ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) are cut or softened at the Feb 2027 guide under a new CFO. FY27 EPS lands ~$13.3 (8% below the $14.44 consensus), NTM ~$13.9, and the stock de-rates to Verizon's multiple: 13.9 x 8.3x (VZ 8.23x [25]) = ~$115. 2027 buybacks shrink to preserve room for spectrum.

base.story: 2026 guidance is delivered and 2027 comes in slightly below the framework (Core EBITDA ~$39-40B, AFCF ~$19.5B). Buybacks take the share count to ~1,020M. SpaceX stays a narrative overhang but not a P&L event by Oct 2027: the Grain spectrum needs FCC approval and a terrestrial build, and SpaceX lacks an MVNO. The multiple settles at ~10.7x NTM EPS of ~$15.06, an ~8% premium to verified peers that the growth slope supports: ~$161.

bull.story: The threat fades (FCC delay, no MVNO, SpaceX focuses elsewhere). Q3/Q4 show churn normalising and strong account adds, the 2027 framework is reaffirmed at the midpoint, and a large 2027 return program is executed at depressed prices. The stock re-rates toward ~13.25x NTM EPS of ~$15.5 (TMUS traded at 11.82x even after the shock [1]): ~$205. This needs no Deutsche Telekom offer, which is excluded as unverified.

comps_summary.peer_range: Core set of 8 (VZ, T, CMCSA, RCI, BCE, TU, VOD, AMX): forward P/E 5.90x (CMCSA) to 15.46x (TU), median 9.95x; trailing lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA 4.58x (CMCSA) to 9.72x (TU), median 7.38x. With CHTR and DTEGY included (round-1 set of 10) the medians are 9.91x and 6.91x, so the P/E anchor barely moves. Fewer than 10 genuine, verifiable large-cap wireless comparables exist once the distressed and circular names are removed.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 10.75x NTM P/E (+8% vs 9.95x; TMUS today 11.82x). 6.6x company-basis EV/LTM Core EBITDA, which is 7.75x on the peer basis (+5% vs 7.38x; TMUS today 8.06x). 11.75% FCF yield (VZ 12.44%, T 11.62%; TMUS today 11.54%). All inside the peer ranges.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The premium is sized from verified data, not from sell-side outperformance calls. Among the two US national peers, the forward P/E rises ~0.24x per point of 3Y EPS growth (VZ 8.23x at 6.99%, T 9.20x at 11.06%). TMUS's 17.03% forecast implies ~10.6x, an ~8% premium to the 9.95x median. I expect that premium to persist through the horizon because the growth gap rests on reported operating data: Q2 service revenue +9% and Core EBITDA +12% [15], a maintained 2027 framework [18][19], and leverage of 2.3x below the 2.5x target [16][18]. I cap it below the supervisor's ~10% and well below the historic premium for three reasons. Part of the EPS growth is buybacks. Consensus revenue growth for 2027 is only +4.44% [2]. And the growth premium is exactly what SpaceX and cable contest: account adds fell to a guided ~250k in Q3 [23], and cable MVNO switcher share rose [11]. AMX at 10.9x on 18% growth [33] also bounds it.

thesis_break_reason: $115 is ~8.2x my FY27 EPS of $14.01 (the $14.44 consensus less 3%), about Verizon's 8.23x forward P/E [25]. It is also a ~15.8% yield on the low end of 2027 AFCF guidance per current share ($19.5B / 1,072.7M = $18.18) [18][17]. A sustained trade there would mean the market has given up TMUS's growth premium and the 2027 framework: a cut to the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets at the Feb 2027 guide, account adds well below the 950k-1.05M 2026 guide after the Q3 churn bump, or a credible SpaceX route to scale before 2028 (an MVNO with a major carrier, or FCC approval plus an aggressive terrestrial launch). That is my bear case happening, not ordinary volatility: it is ~23% below spot, about 0.8 sigma at 33% vol.

Expiry of the $18.2B 2026 stockholder-return authorization; size of the 2027 program within the 'up to ~$30B' framework

key_uncertainties: How fast SpaceX can turn EchoStar 2 GHz plus Grain 800 MHz into a competitive mobile service. The low band is not compatible with V1/V2 satellites (New Street) and is mainly a terrestrial base layer, and Moffett says SpaceX needs an MVNO from one of the Big Three [5]. Whether that matters before Oct 2027 is the swing factor for the multiple.
Whether the 2027 framework ($40-41B Core EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF) survives the Feb 2027 guide under a new CFO, given consensus 2027 revenue growth of only +4.44%.
Reduced disclosure: no postpaid phone net adds since Q1 2026, so deterioration is harder to see early [11].
Size and pace of 2027 buybacks. My count assumes ~$7B of 2027 buybacks; spectrum spending could crowd them out.
Controlled-company governance: DT holds 53.7% of votes, SoftBank has a VPF on 10M shares [21], and a DT holdco deal may not pay minorities a premium.
Management turnover: CBPO departure (July 2026) and the CFO transition (Feb 2027) [19][20].
Price-lock litigation and arbitration (Oddo v. T-Mobile) [14]: reputational more than financial so far.
Rates: a leveraged dividend payer is sensitive to long yields (not quantified by me in this round).
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed most of my round-1 inputs (EPS $14.44, company-basis net debt $84.1B plus $3.46B towers, ~1,020M horizon shares) and flagged three things, all now acted on. (1) My 2027 Core EBITDA of $38.8B silently sat below the company's 2027 target. I reopened the Feb 2026 8-K [18] ($40.0-41.0B EBITDA, $19.5-20.5B AFCF, capex $9-10B, up to ~$30B of returns through 2027, 2.5x leverage target) and the 2026-09-03 8-K [19] ('maintains its capital return program and long-term financial framework'). I now use guidance with an explicit 2% haircut to the low end ($39.2B) and label the $19.5B AFCF as guidance (low end). (2) The sell-side evidence came via Stocktwits recaps. The target actions are now cited from StockAnalysis [2] (Scotiabank $217->$212 on Oct 9; Bernstein Hold $220), and no multiple or haircut is set by them. (3) Whether 10.5x leaves too little premium: I derived the premium from the verified VZ/T growth-multiple slope, which gives ~10.6x, and use 10.75x. I also removed the keyed Twelve Data quote URL (source 1 is now the StockAnalysis statistics page, which shows the same close, $148.58 / -13.27%), dropped a stale 2024 KeyBanc note, and moved CHTR (distressed) and DTEGY (circular) out of the peer medians. Bear evidence still weighed: SpaceX's Grain deal (FCC approval pending, terrestrial layer, Recon: 'not an if; it's a when') [5]; slowing operations (Q3 guide: ~250k account adds, EBITDA +8%, elevated churn from the plan migration [23]; ARPA +2% [16]); reduced disclosure [11]; litigation [14]; management turnover [19][20]; DT control and the SoftBank VPF [21]. Checked and not found: material insider selling (latest Form 144 is 772 shares [22]); a short campaign (short interest 2.94% of float [1]); leverage stress (2.3x company basis [16]; Altman Z of 1.8 on StockAnalysis [1] is typical for a capital-intensive carrier and is not a red flag by itself). Credit ratings and bond spreads still could not be confirmed at a reopenable source and are left out. Valuation: P/E $161.9 (0.40), FCF yield $162.7 (0.35), EV/EBITDA $159.9 (0.25), giving fair value ~$162 (round 1: $154). Scenarios: bear $115 (25%), base $161 (55%), bull $205 (20%), expected $158.3. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those prices (log sd 0.23 / 0.17 / 0.17), with tails floored for gap risk: 0.25 x 115 + 0.55 x 161 + 0.20 x 205 = 158.3, median ~$157, P(>= $149) = 0.585. The overall dispersion (~27% log sd) is a bit under the 33% realized vol, because realized vol includes the one-off shock. The upper tail stays thin (P(>= $223) = 0.08): it would need ~14.5x NTM EPS, which needs a strategic event I cannot verify. The sell-side average target of $241.5 [2] is stale relative to the shock and has been cut repeatedly, so it is a sentiment marker, not an anchor. Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep a 3% haircut to FY27 consensus EPS, a +8% rather than +10% P/E premium, and the low end of AFCF guidance at an 11.75% yield rather than 11.5%. These are skeptic-lane judgments that consensus does not yet reflect the slowdown visible in the company's own Q3 guide. Lane: 15 of 34 sources are in-lane; excluding the 10 peer-statistics pages the comps rule requires, 15 of 24 (63%). sec.gov refused scripted access with a generic User-Agent, so I read the filings with WebFetch. Note 12 of the 10-Q was past the fetch limit, so the remaining 2026 authorization (~$8.5B) is my estimate from the Q2 release and the 10-Q equity statement.
